While working with our partner centers/institutes, students will be challenged with real problems faced by today’s industries, gaining valuable application development and research experience. They are expected to confidently and innovatively apply what they have learned.

name: Capstone Project
description: In partial fulfillment of the degree requirements, each MScomputing student must complete a capstone project with a SIS Faculty, an aligned institute, center or lab. While working with our partner centers/institutes, students will be challenged with real problems faced by today’s industries, gaining valuable application development and research experience. They are expected to confidently and innovatively apply what they have learned.

name: Business Appl. of Digital Tech
description: Technologies play an important enabling role in digital transformation by improving efficiency and increasing productivity. As new disruptive know-hows continue to be developed, it is vital to keep up to date on the state-of-the-art knowledge in advanced science and digital technology. In this module, you will learn about use cases and best practices in enabling technologies such as data science, artificial intelligence, mobile and wearables, blockchain, 5G and communication technologies, cloud computing, IoT, social computing, and APIs/microservices.

name: Digital Org. & Change Mgmt
description: In a rapidly changing business environment driven by digitalisation, an organisation must continually adapt and take advantage of new opportunities to avoid being left behind. To thrive in such an environment, the organisation must be able to adopt new approaches to working and develop a strong change culture. A skilled and change-ready workforce is a key factor for successful digitalisation or IT change. The effective application of change management and communication techniques will significantly improve the chance of success for digital transformation initiatives. Thus, executives who are leading change management teams must be equipped with the necessary competencies and appropriate toolkit to embark on the transformation journey.Organisations are led, managed and run by people. People is a key and fundamental factor for any organisational change to occur. To successfully transition into a new digital model, the people need to be empowered and the organisation aligned to the digital strategy. In this module, you will learn about digital talent management, principles of effective organisational change management, vision and case for change, key stakeholder management, communication and training management, and sustaining culture change.

name: Agile & DevSecOps
description: Traditional waterfall approach to software development is not flexible enough to support digital strategies to deliver business results fast. Organisations need to become more agile in systems analysis and design beyond a linear sequential flow. Adopting DevSecOps delivers business value by increasing the speed of application releases to production, thereby, shortening the time to market. In this module, you will learn about Agile principles and model, DevSecOps practices and large-scale experimentation (A/B-testing) approach.

name: (digital) Product Management
description: Enterprises are increasingly turning to digital innovation and investments to drive business growth. A key aspect involves digital product management playing a crucial role in orchestrating different stakeholders to drive digital business success. However, shifting from a project-centric to a product-centric model requires major changes to the existing enterprise. In the module, you will learn the fundamentals of product management, business model canvas, pricing and segmentation, digital product life cycle, and managing a product development team.

name: Digital Governance & Risk Mgmt
description: Digital governance is a subset of corporate governance that balances conformance and performance in objective setting and decision making for the digital enterprise. To achieve this outcome, management requires an enterprise-wide view of IT risks to articulate the potential risk impact on the business outcomes. Information security incidents generate a high level of anxiety associated with a fear of the unknown. In this module, you will learn about information security, digital governance styles and mechanisms, data policies and procedures, and risk management concepts and framework.

name: Exp. Learning & Design Think'g
description:
Digital transformation is about reinventing business practices. With rapid changes and improvement of digital technology, organisations must be innovative in integrating technologies to enhance customer experience. The shift from business as usual to digital first is not an easy task. Leaders and managers must be able to continually generate fresh and sustain the level of innovation. Keeping up with the competition can present a challenge and leave many unsure of how to proceed. Very often, digital transformation projects present challenges that are complex and undefined. Experimentation and design thinking provide a simple approach to tackle such business challenges.

Human-centred design is critical in the digital world. The digital systems developed must address the fundamental needs and requirements of the user. Design thinking can be used to bring about digital innovations. Through empathy, ideation, prototyping and testing, new solutions can be rapidly co-created, experimented and enhanced in an iterative process. In this module, you will learn about business experimentation, design thinking process, ethnographic methods, customer journey mapping, systems thinking and user experience design (UX).

name: Digital Enterpr. Architecture
description: Delivering business outcomes requires strong collaboration among different individuals and teams across the organisation. An enterprise architecture roadmap is sometimes used to illustrate the milestones, deliverables and investments required to manage change to a future state from the current state over a specific period for such outcomes. In the module, you will learn architecture principles and lifecycle methodology, different types of architecture viz. business, data and information, application and new technologies (e.g. cloud, analytics, IoT).

name: Digital Tech & Sustainability
description:
We are falling short to meet the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030. Digital technologies have disrupted many areas of our lives, but can it accelerate the world towards living more sustainably?

Journey through this course to unpack concepts related to sustainability and digital technologies such as AI, Blockchain and IoT. Dive into use cases where technologies have established breakthroughs in furthering the SDG goals across diverse sectors such as food, energy, well-being, poverty and education.

Understand the unique roles that governments, the private sector, non profit and consumers like yourself play. Be inspired and equipped towards a career involving the intersection of the economy, society and sustainability. Afterall, businesses are here to stay and there are no alternatives planets just yet.

name: Blockchain Technology
description: This course explores the technology of blockchains and smart contracts. The fundamentals of blockchains and smart contracts are first explained and then the similarities and differences of public and private blockchains are shown. Various blockchain platforms are considered as well as the end-to-end implementation of a range of services, for example media rights and supply chains. The course has hands-on development, deployment and execution of smart contracts using Solidity for Ethereum. Emphasis is placed throughout the course on analysing real-world situations using case studies and gaining hands-on experience with coding smart contracts. Guest speakers from companies using blockchains and blockchain vendors will share their experiences.

name: Comp Thinking with Python
description: Problem-solving for real-word issues involves systematically approaching problems and devising solutions that can be executed through a computer program. Computational thinking, as the pivotal skill for problem-solving, can be applied to solve a wide range of problems with quantitative and strategic constraints.In this course, students will acquire proficiency in the Python programming language with the objective of problem-solving using computational thinking, which includes decomposition, pattern recognition, and abstraction. By the end of the course, students will be able to create concise Python programs to solve computational problems in specific contexts.

name: RPA for Business Applications
description:
Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is gaining traction across various industries and holds significant potential for diverse business applications.

This course is designed to familiarize students with RPA tools and guide them in implementing RPA processes tailored to different business domains.

name: Stat Thinking for Data Science
description:
Recent technological advances have enabled more seamless ways of generating and collecting larger volumes and varieties of data. Statistical Thinking, a crucial branch of Mathematics, serves as the cornerstone for visualising, analysing, interpreting, and predicting outcomes from the data. Descriptive Statistics forms the foundation by providing fundamental tools for summarising data, while Inferential Statistics empowers us to draw inferences and deductions about broader populations based on sampled data.

In this course, students will learn to explore and present data to discover underlying patterns and trends, apply statistical thinking and computing to analyse data, and convert them into meaningful information using Python programming. The first half of each lesson will be dedicated to equipping students with statistical thinking concepts, while the second half will be focused on the practical aspects of implementing the concepts using Python and applying them to Data Science problem statements.

name: Modern Software Solution Dev
description: Constructing/deploying large-scale software solutions to support ever-changing business needs has been a challenging problem. Modern software solutions often need to incorporate emerging AI services such as large language models, computer vision, audio analytics, etc., to deliver better values and insights for businesses. In this course, students will learn the fundamentals of software engineering, focusing on the integration of new AI services and applications into modern software systems. Students will experience building and deploying a scalable and extensible software system using a component-based design, microservices architecture, and cloud-native technologies.

name: Digitalisation and Process Inn
description:
Processes are a series of structured and coordinated activities that an organisation performs to achieve specific business outcomes. Business processes form a vital aspect of an organisation’s capability to compete in the market. Very often, processes are the basis where digital transformation happen. Process thinking can be a helpful tool to help organisation to achieve quantum improvements in business goals.  Techniques are applied to eliminate non-value add activities, redefine job roles and streamline information flow. 

With advances in digital technologies, the potential impacts of redesigned process are further enhanced. These digital technologies allow the redesigned processes to be implemented more speedily and with higher accuracy. Digital technologies enhance process improvement initiatives leading to greater innovations to exceed customer needs and lower costs. In this module, you will learn about core business processes, process thinking, and mapping, analysing and redesigning processes with and without applying digital technologies.

name: Web3 Fundamentals
description:
With the advent of Bitcoin, a cryptographically-enabled peer-to-peer digital payment system, blockchain together with a whole package of distributed ledger technologies have been gaining attention from both academia and industry in the last decade. Furthermore, the recent years have witnessed tremendous momentum in the development of a whole cluster of technologies including blockchain and distributed ledger technologies, privacy-enhancing computation, data pricing, data auditing among others, largely due to the impressive rise in the market capital of these digital tokens and the growth of digital economy. This cluster of technologies addresses primarily two core pillars of collaborative intelligence and tokenized economy, which are usually termed trendily as “Web3”.  More and more industries, from banking and insurance, to supply chain and e-commerce, are quickly realizing the great potential in Web3 technology in efficiency boost, process automation and secure data sharing across otherwise isolated data silos. Web3 is set to nurture a whole set of new economies. 

This course introduces you to the Web3 ecosystem, from concept to evolution, from technologies to applications. Students will learn the defining characteristics of Web3 technologies and learn to design, develop and evaluate the application of Web3 technologies in various settings for problem solving.

This course is intended for students with little or no programming experience.

name: Low Code App Development
description: Low Code Application Platforms (LCAP) are trending in industry.  Government agencies in Singapore now require LCAP in their software outsource requirements, including for public facing applications.  Both major Telco’s in Singapore are using LCAP.  Banks are ramping up their adoption of LCAP.  This course exposes students to LCAP using OutSystems, a leading LCAP provider.  The course starts out covering architecture and design best practices, followed by weekly hands-on lab exercises covering data modeling, processing logic, API development, and user interface development.  Student teams will develop a complete application for their term project. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop commercial-grade full-stack applications without writing any code.

name: Sustainable IT Sys & Practices
description:
This course, Sustainable IT Systems and Practices, is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of sustainable digital transformation strategies. It covers key topics such as carbon footprint analysis of digital infrastructure, green software development, green cloud migration strategies, circular economy principles in technology lifecycle management, and metrics for measuring sustainability ROI in transformation projects. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, ensuring students can apply these concepts to real-world challenges. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, case studies, and group projects, students will gain insights into the latest innovations and best practices in sustainable digital architecture design.

The course is tailored for junior to mid-management level professionals in the IT and business sectors who are interested in integrating sustainability into their digital transformation strategies. This includes IT managers, digital transformation leaders, sustainability officers, and business analysts seeking to enhance their skills in designing and implementing sustainable digital architectures. The course is also suitable for professionals from related fields who wish to expand their knowledge of sustainable digital technologies and their applications in business environments. By focusing on practical skills and real-world applications, the course prepares students to lead sustainable digital initiatives within their organisations, aligning business goals with environmental sustainability.

name: Python Programming
description: This is a centrally-coordinated shared course, which can be considered as an open course to count towards your graduation requirement, when applicable.Many real-world businesses require data analysts, data engineers and data scientists to build applications in programming language Python, together with several off-the-shelf libraries. This course is designed for students who wish to master Python as a programming language and build data analysis solutions with Python along with several widely used libraries. This course teaches both the Python programming language itself and how to carry out descriptive and diagnostic data analysis in Python. In the Python programming part, basic topics including data types, containers and control flow will first be introduced. As advanced topics in Python programming, lambda expressions, functions, modules and regular expressions will also be explained and elaborated in great details. In the second part, this course will teach functions in the three important libraries numpy, pandas and matplotlib. With these three libraries, students are then ready to perform descriptive and diagnostic data analysis with data visualization on sample datasets provided by the course instructors. Upon the completion of the course, students should be able to carry out data analysis with Python and related libraries at a high proficient level.

name: Global Exposure Project
description: The Global Exposure Project (GEP) is a joint initiative between MITB and Sogang University, offered as a 1 CU practicum module, over a 5-week period during the July Term of the academic calendar. This immersive, cross-institutional module is structured to cultivate collaboration, innovation, and hands-on problem-solving.Its core objective is to strengthen students’ problem-solving capabilities by engaging them with real-world industry challenges, exposing them to international business ecosystems, and fostering cross-cultural teamwork. Students will tackle practical issues faced by high-tech companies through a capstone project that blends academic rigor with industry relevance, preparing them to thrive in global, innovation-driven environments. For a start, the problems will have fintech, data science and digital transformation focus.

name: Threat Intell & Incident Resp
description: This course provides a comprehensive foundation for transforming raw security data into actionable, strategic intelligence. In the initial weeks, we will establish the core principles of CTI, differentiating it from simple Indicators of Compromise (IoCs) and defining its critical role within a larger organisational risk management strategy. You will be guided through the formal Intelligence Cycle, focusing on the crucial \"Direction\" phase by learning how to define Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs). We will conduct deep dives into foundational analytical models—the Cyber Kill Chain, the Pyramid of Pain, and the Diamond Model—to build a systematic understanding of attack scenarios, and you will immediately apply these concepts using practical tools like VirusTotal to analyse and process raw threat data.As the course progresses, we shift focus from foundational theory to advanced analysis and practical application. We will dedicate significant time to understanding adversarial motivations, profiling key threat actor categories (from nation-states to insider threats), and mastering the industry-standard MITRE ATT&CK Framework to map and measure defensive gaps. The second half of the course emphasises the crucial integration of CTI into the Incident Response (IR) Lifecycle, demonstrating how intelligence provides maximum value during the Identification and Containment phases of a security incident. The curriculum culminates in a hands-on Capture the Flag group exercise and a final Group Presentation, where you will demonstrate your ability to analyse, process, and effectively disseminate finished intelligence products to enable proactive cyber defence.

name: Enterprise Cryptography
description: Cryptography is the cornerstone of modern cybersecurity infrastructures. Enterprise Cryptography provides a comprehensive exploration of cryptographic principles, technologies, and deployment practices essential for securing modern information systems. The course bridges foundational cryptography with real-world enterprise applications, focusing on how cryptographic technologies are used to protect data, services, and infrastructure in public and private sectors.Students will study core primitives, such as symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hash functions, digital signatures, key exchange, and cryptographic protocols in enterprise systems, such as TLS, IPSec, S/MIME, Kerberos, and FIDO2. The course will also introduce advanced cryptographic primitives and tools that play a key role in ensuring data security and privacy in emerging and future applications, including Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs), such as multi-party computation (MPC), fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP), as well as Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), which can resist attacks by both classical computers and future quantum computers.By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of modern cryptography and be equipped with practical skills to evaluate cryptographic solutions, architect secure systems, and make informed decisions about cryptographic strategies within an enterprise.

name: Strategic Cybersecurity Mgmt
description: In today’s digital economy, cybersecurity is no longer a purely technical function; it is a strategic business capability. Organisations are facing unprecedented cyber risks arising from cloud adoption, digital transformation, AI-driven threats, supply-chain dependency, and increasingly complex regulatory obligations. Cybersecurity leaders must therefore be able to connect technical security principles with enterprise-level strategy, governance, and risk decision-making.This course is structured around weekly modules that cover essential topics in enterprise security risk management, the formulation and enforcement of IT security policies, and the implementation of secure architecture and software development practices using AWS cloud services. By progressing through these areas, students will build a comprehensive understanding of how to evaluate, design, and manage security solutions that align with business priorities in modern organizations.Modern cyber incidents have direct financial, operational, and reputational consequences. Boards and senior executives expect cybersecurity leaders to:•	Assess enterprise cyber risks in business terms•	Align security controls with strategic objectives and regulatory compliance•	Incorporate robust security measures into cloud-based systems.

name: Info Storage & Retrieval
description:
This course studies the theory, design and implementation of data management and information retrieval systems. The data management portion covers indexing, query processing, transaction management, and XML. The information retrieval component of the course includes important retrieval models (Boolean, vector space, probabilistic), relevance feedback, and web search engines.

Pre-requisites:
- IS202: Data Management or Equivalent
- Undergraduate-Level: Probability & Statistics

name: Research Apprenticeship
description:
This module is intended to equip Ph.D. students for research. Each student will work with a faculty mentor to carry out literature survey and identify potential thesis topics. 

By the end of the second term, a students should have delivered at least a survey/research paper or grant proposal. Students will continue to register for this module until they pass the thesis proposal, which must be completed within 4 terms. 

The mentor will assign a grade at the end of each term, based on the student's research progress.

name: Foundations for IS & Mgmt Res
longName: Foundations for IS and Management Research
description: The course aims to offer graduate students an overview of fundamental research methodologies in information systems and management. It covers concepts from various areas such as microeconomics, econometrics, optimization, stochastic process, and game theory. Students will be exposed to topics such as the strategic role of IT, business value of IT, strategic alignment of IT, IT outsourcing, IS capabilities, competencies and leadership. With the knowledge acquired during this course, students will be able to identify, formulate, and analyze their interested ISM research question.

name: Human-Computer Interaction
description: This course introduces fundamental human-computer interaction principles and techniques for designing usable interactive systems. Topics include human perception and performance, methods for gathering user requirements, prototyping methods, and evaluation methods. This course is intended for anyone who wants to learn how to design usable systems, and will be of interest to students in information systems, psychology, and business (marketing). Students will design a user interface throughout the course, but no visual design or programming skill required.

name: Network Analysis and Mining
description:
This course delves into research and survey papers in graph mining, social network mining and social information retrieval, with an emphasis on system and application issues. Topics to be covered include graph and network databases, graph mining, social network analysis, link prediction, community detection, and social behavior mining.

The course is intended to prepare graduate students for research in data mining, information retrieval or text mining.
areas: MScC Data Science & Engineering Track Core
PhD CS Artificial Intelligence & Data Science Core
MScC Software & Cyber-Physical Systems Track Elect

name: Systems and Data Security
description: This course introduces graduate students to advanced topics in information security, with first seven weeks focusing on system security and the last seven weeks focusing on data security. The topics to be covered in system security include buffer overrun attacks and defenses, denial of service attacks and their defenses, network- and host-based intrusion detection, secure Internet routing, and binary analysis. The topics to be covered in data security include RFID privacy notions and their relations, data protection in EPCglobal network, secure and flexible data access in the Cloud, inference control and auditing, and privacy preserving data mining.

name: Foundations for Data Analytics
description:
The overall objective of this course is to familiarize the PHD students with data analytics and its applicability in a real business environment. Here, data analytics include the extensive use of data, statistical and quantitative analysis, exploratory and predictive models, and fact-based simulation. The class mainly deals with empirical fundamentals for data analytics. Knowing how to effectively use them (method for data analytics) to solve research problems will be very helpful in PHD students’ future professional career.

We will study (1) how to systematically understand what you see and (2) how to make what you believe more persuasive. Data analytic tools will be very useful in many situations you are confronted with. The class will be built on applied economics, statistics, and applied econometrics.
areas: MScC Data Science & Engineering Track Core
PhD CS Information Systems & Technology Core
PhD CS Artificial Intelligence & Data Science Core
MScC Software & Cyber-Physical Systems Track Elect

name: Data Security
description: This course introduces graduate students to some advanced topics in data security, including RFID privacy notions and their relations, data protection in EPCglobal network, RFID clone detection, RFID path authentication, data access in the Cloud, IBE and fuzzy IBE, KP-ABE, CP-ABE, and inference control and auditing.
areas: PhD CS Information Systems & Technology Core

name: Library Training I
description:
SMU Library offers comprehensive research skill training such as Avoiding Plagiarism through APA Citation, Literature Review, Current Awareness, Research Data Management, Research Impact, and academic publishing etc.
Library Trainings form part of the foundational research skills and methodology training for the doctoral student to embark on their research journey.

name: Library Training II
description:
SMU Library offers comprehensive research skill training such as Avoiding Plagiarism through APA Citation, Literature Review, Current Awareness, Research Data Management, Research Impact, and academic publishing etc.
Library Trainings form part of the foundational research skills and methodology training for the doctoral student to embark on their research journey.

name: Empirical Research Project I
description: The ERP could be a small industry project or a pre-dissertation topic, or to survey a paper. The deliverables can be a case study or short paper (5 pages), a system implementation or a demo of an algorithm. The duration of the ERP should be 15 weeks

description: The ERP could be a small industry project or a pre-dissertation topic, or to survey a paper. The deliverables can be a case study or short paper (5 pages), a system implementation or a demo of an algorithm. The duration of the ERP should be 15 weeks.

name: Research Seminars I
description:
This is a 0.5 CU Research Seminars module for EngD students. Students are required to attend at least 5 seminars per AY which can come from the following:

•	Translational research seminar delivered by industry professionals, visiting researchers or faculty members
•	Graduating PhD in IS/CS and EngD (pre-conference talks)
•	MITB Monthly Seminars/In-Conversation Series
•	MITB AI Translational Research Seminars

Students are required to submit a 2-3 page learning journal at the end of the AY (upon attending at least 5 seminars) about their reflections of the seminars and how the knowledge acquired can be applied to their own practice research setting.

Students are required to submit a 2-3 page learning journal at the end of the AY (upon attending at least 5 seminars) about their reflections of the seminars and how the knowledge acquired can be applied to their own practice research setting.

name: Scient. Writing & Presentation
description: The Scientific Writing course teaches topics on clarity, fluidity, conciseness, and organization in scientific writing. Scientific Presentation course covers Engaging audience by meeting expectations and presentation goals; Presenting the TED way; Redesigning slides for ease of understanding & impact; Presenting to an expert audience with technical slides; and Handling Q&A with difficult questions.

name: Web3 and Tokenised Economy
description:
This course provides a rigorous and practice-oriented introduction to Web3 and the tokenised economy, with a focus on their technological foundations, economic logic, application landscape, and strategic implications for business and society. It examines the broader shift toward a digital economy in which computing becomes increasingly ubiquitous, decentralised, and collaborative, and explores how Web3 seeks to address two fundamental requirements of this transition: decentralised trust and sustainable incentive mechanisms.  

Students will study the core components of the Web3 ecosystem, including the cryptographic and consensus foundations that enable data integrity and decentralised coordination. The course also introduces token taxonomy, token-based and token-less application models, and the design logic of tokenised systems. Particular attention is given to decentralised finance (DeFi), including its historical development, key primitives, and representative use cases such as lending, stablecoins, prediction markets, and decentralised exchanges.  

Beyond technical and application-level understanding, the course emphasizes critical evaluation and executive relevance. Students will learn approaches to tokenomics design, frameworks for assessing Web3 projects, and major issues relating to compliance, regulation, and future development. Through discussion, reflection, ecosystem exposure, and project presentation, the course equips DBA(Tech) participants to critically analyse Web3 innovations and assess their implications for business strategy, governance, and digital transformation.

name: Advanced Topic in DB and IR
longName: Advanced Topic in Database and Information Retrieval
description: This course delves into research and survey papers in database and information retrieval, with an emphasis on system and application issues. Topics to be covered include spatial database, data integrity and privacy, indexing, information retrieval models, relevance feedback, and multimedia information retrieval. The course is intended to prepare graduate students for research in data management and information retrieval.

name: Adv. Topics in Info. Security
description: This course introduces graduate students to advanced topics in information security, with first seven weeks focusing on system security and the last seven weeks focusing on data security. The topics to be covered in system security include buffer overrun attacks and defenses, denial of service attacks and their defenses, network- and host-based intrusion detection, secure Internet routing, and binary analysis. The topics to be covered in data security include RFID privacy notions and their relations, data protection in EPCglobal network, secure and flexible data access in the Cloud, inference control and auditing, and privacy preserving data mining.

name: Adv Topics in Int Systems
description:
Intelligent systems are being employed in many walks of life ranging from software personal assistants in office environments to assisting in patrolling critical infrastructure, providing financial advice to helping avoid queues at theme parks, and so on. This course covers advanced topics in building these intelligent systems that make decisions or provide support to humans in making decisions. Furthermore, the topics explored are at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Operations Research (Management Science). More specifically, we will provide real world applications and the theoretical underpinnings for the following topics:
• Reasoning with Uncertainty 
  > Graphical Models (Bayesian networks, etc.) 
        - Representation and Inference
        - Machine Learning from a probabilistic perspective
  > Decision making 
        - Planning
        - Scheduling
• Reasoning with Multiple Agents (MAS)
   > Cooperative Settings
         - Distributed Constraint optimization
         - Multi-agent Markov Models
   > Competitive Settings
         - Game Theory
         - Auctions and Mechanism Design

name: Research Paper
description:
This module is intended for PhD students to demonstrate their research potential, and constitutes a major milestone in their progress through the PhD program.

Each student is required to complete an original research report. The work should be substantial enough to lead to one or more papers that are publishable at good conference or journal venues, with minor extension in the technical content and (likely significant) polishing in the presentation. It will form the foundation for the dissertation proposal.

name: Research and Thesis
